headline: Sellers Swept the Floor on Wednesday as Only One Sector Escaped Meaningful Damage
body_html:
Wednesday's session was a broad retreat, with 406 stocks falling against just 136 rising across the 544-name universe. Homebuilders led the damage, surrendering roughly 3 percent on the day, while Materials stocks gave back more than 2.4 percent and Industrials dropped 2.1 percent. The selling was wide enough to clip Semiconductors by nearly 1.8 percent and Consumer names by 1.4 percent, leaving Healthcare as the lone sector to hold near flat, off only a quarter of a point.

Geopolitical unease supplied a ready narrative. Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest weekly pace since the start of the Iran conflict, and the International Energy Agency signaled it would accelerate releases from strategic reserves — a move implying that supply disruption risk is real enough to warrant preemptive action. Energy shares fell 1.16 percent despite the backdrop, suggesting traders viewed the IEA response as demand-dampening rather than price-supportive.

Glaukos and Progyny, both Healthcare names, topped the leaderboard with gains of 6.55 percent and 6.33 percent respectively, underlining the defensive tilt. Micron's 4.06 percent advance stood out as the semiconductor exception, buoyed by fresh analyst optimism over a potential repeat of its prior earnings surge. Heading into Thursday, the path of least resistance still appears to favor defensive positioning until Middle East tensions show a credible sign of easing.

briefs.headline: Micron Bucks the Chip Selloff With a 4 Percent Advance
briefs.body: Micron climbed 4.06 percent on Wednesday even as the broader Semiconductor sector slid nearly 1.8 percent, lifted by a boldly bullish analyst argument that the memory chipmaker could deliver another outsized earnings run. Market observers noted partial agreement with the bull case while flagging execution risks that temper full conviction.

briefs.headline: IEA Move on Reserves Signals Deep Concern Over Hormuz Disruption
briefs.body: The International Energy Agency said it would speed up releases from strategic petroleum stockpiles, with roughly 100 million barrels still in the pipeline. The announcement came as sources reported that tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz reached their highest weekly count since hostilities with Iran began, rattling energy markets despite a 1.16 percent sector decline.

briefs.headline: Hezbollah Said to Receive $200 Million From Iran for Displaced Populations
briefs.body: Exclusive reports indicate that Iran has directed approximately $200 million to Lebanon's Hezbollah to assist people displaced by ongoing conflict. The disclosure adds another layer to a widening regional crisis that is already driving elevated risk premiums across Middle Eastern shipping lanes and influencing global commodity sentiment.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Bear the Steepest Sector Loss of the Session
briefs.body: The Homebuilders group fell 3 percent on Wednesday, the sharpest decline of any sector tracked. The drop reflects sustained pressure from rate-sensitive consumer spending and may also echo broader macro caution as geopolitical headlines stoke uncertainty. No comparable relief catalyst was visible heading into Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Glaukos and Progyny Offer a Healthcare Safe Haven
briefs.body: Eye-care device maker Glaukos surged 6.55 percent and fertility-benefits firm Progyny rose 6.33 percent, making Healthcare the session's defensive anchor. The pair's outperformance illustrates how investors rotated toward sub-industries insulated from commodity costs and geopolitical supply shocks when broad risk appetite deteriorated sharply.

briefs.headline: Middle East Diplomacy Shifts as Turkey Backs Saudi Arabia Against Houthis
briefs.body: Turkey confirmed it is supplying technical and defensive support to Saudi Arabia in its campaign against Houthi forces in Yemen, while separate reports indicate Syria is weighing whether to extend military assistance to Riyadh as well. The diplomatic realignment underscores the expanding regional dimension of the conflict and adds uncertainty to energy-supply forecasts.
